speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the infant is presenting with bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance, which raises concern for intestinal obstruction. When did these symptoms first begin, and has the baby passed any stool since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor

text: The "double bubble" sign confirms duodenal atresia, which is strongly associated with Down syndrome. Given the missed prenatal care, I need to assess for other dysmorphic features. Does the infant have any physical stigmata of Trisomy 21, such as epicanthal folds, a flat nasal bridge, or single palmar creases?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Although the "double bubble" sign is classic for duodenal atresia, I must rule out malrotation with midgut volvulus, which is a surgical emergency. REQUEST TEST: Upper_GI_Series

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal upper GI series effectively rules out malrotation with volvulus, confirming the diagnosis of duodenal atresia. Given the high association with Down syndrome, I will now assess for other congenital anomalies like congenital heart disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal atresia
